name: Capitalnumbers Infotech Ltd
title: Capitalnumbers Infotech Ltd - 544343 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Services firm with no capacity cycle: FY26 revenue up ~5% to INR105 crore, EBITDA flat at INR35.8 crore, and FY27 guidance of minimum 35% growth rests on acquisition plus unproven organic adds.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore (from INR99.7 crore), with EBITDA flat at INR35.80 crore and FY27 guidance of minimum 35% growth.
summary.overview: FY26 total income grew 9.4% to INR115.60 crore and revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore, which management said was below internal expectations as enterprise decision cycles elongated and large ramp-ups slipped into FY27. EBITDA was INR35.80 crore versus INR35.69 crore, with the margin (31%, computed on total income including other income of about INR10.55 crore) moderating on Middle East investments, Gurgaon expansion, senior hires and AI build-out. PAT fell to INR25.50 crore from INR25.80 crore and basic EPS to INR10.44 from INR11.83, partly on a full-year post-IPO share count. The company remains debt-free with about INR171.3 crore of cash and investments, and announced a proposed acquisition of Epitome Cloud Inc. for about INR40 crore.

segments.name: AI / ML / GenAI
segments.commentary: AI-related revenue exceeded 10% of total company revenue for the first time in FY26. Management said all AI contracts start as fixed-cost discovery and move to T&M on production.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: US approx. 41%, Europe and UK approx. 31%, Middle East approx. 11%, India approx. 10%, rest of world approx. 7%. Management has pulled back Middle East trade-show spend and new-logo acquisition for now.

segments.name: Engagement model
segments.commentary: About 91% of FY26 revenue came from time-and-material engagements; the remaining about 9% was limited-period fixed-cost work.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: minimum 35% revenue growth in INR terms, described by management as a pessimistic case and subject to revision; no split between organic and inorganic.
EBITDA margin to recover gradually toward 33%, with management also referring to at least 200 bps improvement; the margin basis includes other income.
Three-year goal of about INR200 crore top line while maintaining and improving the EBITDA margin.

Epitome Cloud acquisition: consideration about INR40 crore, target revenue about INR28-30 crore, expected to add 25-30% to revenue; completion expected in 8-12 weeks, funded by IPO proceeds and internal accruals with no external debt.
Management plans two to three further acquisitions (AI with fintech or healthtech vertical focus).
Dividend: interim 10% of face value paid and final 10% proposed; management said payout to be around 20-25% of profit. No buyback planned for now.
capex_capacity: Development centres in Kolkata and Gurgaon; Gurgaon is the hub for new senior hires, AI and ML hiring, and management capacity building.
Onsite presence in Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Morocco; Middle East staff are deployed through a third-party provider, which shows up in technical fees.
Epitome Cloud brings about 55 people (7 onsite in US, about 45 in India) and is run as-is post-acquisition; Epitome revenue is about INR28 crore on a CY26 basis.
Management expects to set up a physical office in the US after the acquisition.
Investments in AI capability, leadership hiring and enterprise sales were expensed, not capitalised, per the CFO.
demand_pricing: Client retention about 90%; management expects about 10% churn and net new revenue of INR20-25 crore organically in FY27.
Two Fortune 500 wins in FY26 (life sciences/healthcare with domain analytics and warehouse management; chemicals and materials with UiPath automation).
Nine international trade shows in FY26, six in the Middle East; about 500 qualified leads generated, and deal cycles of 6-12 months mean conversions are still pending.
Trade-show commitments reduced to two or three major events for FY27 with spend redirected to a new outbound demand-gen team and US/UK/Europe events.
Middle East: one of the top five clients is in the region, with BFSI as the only vertical there; the company is holding off on net new logos in the region.
Management cited global economic uncertainty as the biggest sector headwind, plus AI talent availability; it cited increasing demand for AI, cloud modernisation and automation.

qa_highlights.question: Why has organic growth been weak, and what is the acquisition cost and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Epitome is about INR40 crore consideration, INR28-30 crore revenue, and 25-30% of revenue contribution. Organic growth of INR20-25 crore net new is expected after about 10% churn; 35% is the most pessimistic case.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin 31% when the reported EBITDA is about INR25 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the margin uses total income including other income (about INR10.55 crore) as the denominator. Excluding other income the EBITDA margin is about 34%, so the reported 31% is on the total-income basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why were trade-show and marketing costs reduced, and why did other expenses rise about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East trade-show commitments were cut because of the West Asia situation and spend was redirected to demand gen, US/UK/Europe events. Other expenses rose because Middle East staff are supplied via a third party (technical fees) and marketing spend was reallocated, not cut.

qa_highlights.question: What are the parameters for M&A and Epitome's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four criteria: services company with some IP, majority export revenue, profitable and growing, and a technology or domain specialisation. The CFO said targets must have EBITDA margins in line with the company and bring synergy and new technology or manpower. Management said margins would improve post-deal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback given the cash position, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no buyback is planned for now, with capital directed to growth and acquisitions. The CFO said the dividend payout is intended to be about 20-25% of profit, including the final dividend, and a buyback may be reconsidered in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target breakdown and the three-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 35% is a combined organic and inorganic guidance and a three-year aim of INR200 crore top line with a stable or better margin. The CFO said the 'medium term' reference meant one year, for which 35% growth is projected.

risks_watch: Organic growth: FY26 growth was largely from pricing and the Middle East; FY27 depends on INR20-25 crore net new revenue and the slipped large ramp-ups.
Epitome integration: completion in 8-12 weeks and a Salesforce revenue-operations niche with only 7 onsite US staff; the EBITDA impact and the PAT contribution are not disclosed.
Margin: the 33% FY27 target includes other income, so operating margin is lower (about 24% ex-other income per an analyst's calculation); other income of INR10.55 crore is a large share of PBT.
Middle East: the top-five client exposure with teams no longer travelling; BFSI concentration.
Share price weakness below the IPO price and questions on shareholder returns; no buyback planned.
Use of about INR170 crore cash across acquisitions versus organic investment; capital allocation policy not fully defined.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about the miss versus internal expectations and explained it as slipped deal closures and Middle East disruption. The tone turned assertive on the FY27 35% target, the Epitome deal and the acquisition pipeline, but was evasive on share price, buybacks and the organic growth split.
key_quotes: During the second half of financial year '26, we expected elongated enterprise decision-making cycles and delayed ramp -ups in certain large engagements, some of which now shifted into financial year '27.
So the projection that I am giving of 35% is basically the most pessimistic projection and we will revise it as the company -- as the situation evolves in the future.
Financial year 26 was the year of investment, capability building and strategic positioning of the company.
